column1: # Consolidated typed COUNT, SUM, AVG, DISTINCT, sliding, and spill runtime evidence.

column5: Database and window folding live-consume canonical AVG update/result with Int and UInt promoted to the Go decimal sum domain; typed real merge/reset and incoming-before-outgoing slide remain test-only boundaries. Exact Go decimal context breadth, allocator accounting, and every generated type case remain open.

One signed i64 COUNT state now serves ordinary, partial, merge, reset, and outgoing-before-incoming slide paths; temporal EvalTime writes, approximate-count-distinct, Go chunk lifecycle, and allocator deltas remain open.

The specialized exact-integer update/merge state is represented only at its test boundary; canonical live DISTINCT dispatch instead consumes the prerequisite tuple-key authority, which now gives compare-equal decimals such as 1.0 and 1.00 one normalized key. Real, string, duration, temporal encodings and BJKST FarmHash approximate count distinct remain open.

Database and window folding live-consume canonical SQL SUM update/result with Int and UInt promoted to Decimal before accumulation and value-canonical DISTINCT. Typed merge/reset/sliding states remain test-only; exact Go string/temporal coercion, allocator accounting, and all generated type cases remain open.

SUM_INT remains separate signed/unsigned checked states, and test-only slide cases preserve outgoing-before-incoming order so avoidable overflow disappears. Live Database SQL SUM uses the decimal domain instead; exact Go error text/chunk output and allocator deltas remain open.

A test-only reusable spill buffer round-trips count and representable real/decimal sum-count pairs; no live Database/window spill consumer exists. The decimal framing is Rust-owned and not byte-compatible with Go SerializeMyDecimal, and hidden decimal scale plus chunk deserializer lifecycle remain open.
